newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures slide on back of NYMEX gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures slide on back of NYMEX gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent futures moved into the red on Friday afternoon, shedding modest earlier gains, on the back of a sharp drop in NYMEX gasoline, traders said.
July Brent was trading 19 cents a barrel down at $18.13 by 1610 GMT, a few cents off the day's low of $18.10.
June gas oil also slipped, trading at $164.00 a tonne, or $1.75 down. It was trading at about $167.25 before NYMEX opened.

July Brent broke through what some traders said was good support at $18.20 when the contract began to shed its earlier gains after some fund selling on the heating oil contract set into NYMEX shortly after the market opened.
Later gasoline took the lead in moving the complex down.
"It's gasoline taking us down," one trader said.
July Brent was trading about the $18.48 mark before NYMEX opened.

"There is some fund selling in the heating oil (on NYMEX) and it is pulling everything else lower," one trader said as July Brent began to trade at just a few cents above Thursday's close of $18.32 a barrel.
NYMEX July unleaded gasoline, called to open 0.25 to 0.50 cent higher, was trading 1.02 cents a gallon down at 58.80 cents by 1605 GMT.
July heating oil was trading 0.62 cent a gallon down at 52.70 cents.
